return.work: Japanese Fairy Tales: Urashima Taro returns to his village
return.author: traditional tales; collected by Yei Theodora Ozaki
return.locator: Urashima Taro returns to his village; local text normalized characters 51533-52153
return.excerpt: When Urashima heard these strange words he was frightened, and said: “Please, please, you must not joke with me, I am greatly perplexed. I am really Urashima Taro, and I certainly have not lived three hundred years. Till four or five days ago I lived on this spot. Tell me what I want to know without more joking, please.” But the man’s face grew more and more grave, and he answered: “You may or may not be Urashima Taro, I don’t know. But the Urashima Taro of whom I have heard is a man who lived three hundred years ago. Perhaps you are his spirit come to revisit your old home?” “Why do you mock me?” said Urashima.
return.note: Ozaki's literary retelling of a traditional story, not a primary mythographic text.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: In Ozaki's literary retelling of the Urashima folktale, the fisherman returns from the Sea King's palace and finds that three hundred years have passed. Otohime had warned him not to open a box.

narrativeBlocks.title: The warning about the box
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (local English retelling; whitespace normalized): “you will never open this box!” And Urashima promised that he would never, never open the box whatever happened.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: This is a popular folktale retelling, not a primary source for the kami myths in the Kojiki. Its otherworld and time boundary belong to this story's version.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read the source boundary
narrativeBlocks.body: Keep genre and source visible: Ozaki's Japanese Fairy Tales is a collected literary retelling. Do not use Urashima as evidence for the Amaterasu myth or a universal Japanese belief about the afterlife.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Track the promise, the return, and the changed time-scale before interpreting the box as a symbol.
